label: STOPP H1
title: NSAID with past ulcer or stomach bleeding
statement: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) other than COX-2 selective agents with history of peptic ulcer disease or gastrointestinal bleeding, unless with concurrent PPI or H2 antagonist (risk of peptic ulcer relapse).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)
source.citation: O'Mahony D, Cherubini A, Guiteras AR, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632. doi:10.1007/s41999-023-00777-y

plain_summary: An anti-inflammatory pain medicine can cause another ulcer or bleed in someone who has had one before. This criterion flags use without a proton pump inhibitor or H2 antagonist.

medicine_groups.name: NSAIDs other than the COX-2 selective medicines

ibuprofen: Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 2 to 7 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever 7 to 12 Years
Advil Childrens Pain and Fever Relief 2 to 12 Years
Advil Infants Pain and Fever Relief 3 Months to 2 Years
Nurofen for Children 3 Months to 5 Years

medicine_groups.note: Tablets, capsules, liquids, suppositories and injections count. Skin gels, creams and eye drops do not count. Panafen Plus contains ibuprofen with codeine. Celecoxib and etoricoxib are COX-2 selective and are not in this group. Aspirin is not in this group. Vimovo (naproxen with esomeprazole) already holds a stomach-protecting medicine and is not in this group.

medicine_groups.name: Proton pump inhibitors and H2 antagonists
medicine_groups.note: Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: For people aged 65 or older (eligibility unconfirmed if age is unknown) with a systemic Group A NSAID and no Group B supply on overlapping dates or within 60 days of the NSAID supply, report a finding citing the NSAID lines and the condition line for peptic ulcer disease or past gastrointestinal bleeding, or a possible finding naming the missing history if that history is missing or not known. If a Group B medicine is supplied with the NSAID, there is no finding. If the record explicitly excludes both peptic ulcer disease and past gastrointestinal bleeding, there is no finding.

needs_facts.what: History of peptic ulcer disease or gastrointestinal bleeding
needs_facts.meets: A recorded history of peptic ulcer disease or gastrointestinal bleeding

cannot_be_seen: Whether the person has ever had a stomach ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding, and when. Also how often the NSAID is really taken, anti-inflammatory medicines bought without a prescription, and medicines supplied by a hospital or another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: Whether the person has a history of peptic ulcer or gastrointestinal bleeding, and whether the NSAID is still needed or should be given with stomach protection.
